Correct: communication between a client's browser and a web server uses Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP).

questions.stem: A squadron needs processing power, storage, and applications that many airmen can reach on demand from anywhere, delivered remotely over the Internet. MSgt Rush has no staff to maintain hardware, so the squadron must not have to manage the server or any of the infrastructure behind it. Which server type fits this need?

answers.rationale: Correct: a cloud server and all associated infrastructure are managed by the cloud provider, such as Microsoft Azure.
Wrong: a virtual server lets each section administer its own services, which still leaves the squadron managing them.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host on the Local Area Network (LAN) that the squadron would run itself.
Wrong: an application server runs specific programs as middleware; it is not described as managed by an outside provider.

questions.stem: A plant runs a self-contained industrial network with no link to outside networks. MSgt Rush needs to log on remotely from one computer to the plant's devices and execute tasks on them as if sitting at each machine. Because the network is closed, a server type with a known security weakness is acceptable here. Which server type is typically used in this setting?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a terminal server supplies applications to thin clients and workstations; it is not described as limited to industrial networks.
Correct: a Telnet server is typically used only in industrial and self-contained networks because it is not secure.
Wrong: a virtual server re-creates a physical server as Virtual Machines (VMs); it does not provide remote logon to devices.
Wrong: a proxy server mediates between clients and external servers, and this network has no outside link.

questions.stem: A small detachment has one server for six airmen. It hosts the detachment's website, it also handles all printing on the local network, and MSgt Rush sits at it each morning to do administrator work. A new airman asks how to describe this server's role on the network. Which description fits it?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a single-purpose server provides specific services and nothing else, and end users do not sit at it.
Wrong: it does host a website, but a web server alone serves only web pages, not printing and administrator work.
Correct: a multi-purpose (non-dedicated) web server may also act as a print server or the administrator's workstation.
Wrong: a workstation is a personal computer used by a client; this machine serves the site and printing to others.

questions.stem: Five airmen at a deployed site link their laptops with no server present. Each laptop shares one folder with the others while keeping the rest of its files inaccessible, and when one laptop requests a file from another, the second laptop answers as the server. No laptop has more authority than another. Which network model are the airmen using?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a client-server model relies on a dedicated server as intermediary, and this site has no server.
Wrong: a multi-purpose server is one server doing several tasks, but this site has no server at all.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host that clients connect through; no such host exists here.
Correct: in a peer-to-peer model there are no dedicated servers, and each computer can share only some of its resources.

questions.stem: An airman will be posted for weeks at a remote site that has no network and no domain at all. MSgt Rush must issue a device that has its own processor, memory, and drive and that will never connect to a central server during that time. Which device can function completely on its own in that setting?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a thin client relies on the central server for applications, processing, and memory.
Correct: a workstation has all components and can function completely independently of a server or network.
Wrong: a thick client works in a client-server configuration and still pulls data from the central server occasionally.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host that supplies applications to remote clients; it is not a device issued to an airman.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush checks an airman's workstation while it runs a mission planning application opened through a web portal. Only screen images, mouse movements, and keystrokes cross the network, the workstation's processor shows no load from the application, and the whole squadron uses the one copy installed on a shared Windows server. Which desktop virtualization type is in use?

keywords.text: one copy installed on a shared Windows server

answers.rationale: Only the graphical interface, mouse, and keyboard are shared, with no processing on the client and one shared application instance.
This type hosts a dedicated Operating System (OS) Virtual Machine (VM) for each client, not one shared copy.
This model sends portions of the program code to the client, so the client would show processing.
This type moves profiles, settings, and data to a central share; it is not an application delivery method.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must give deployed airmen access to graphics-heavy imagery software from tablets. The design needs hardware-based Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) sharing through a secure connection from any device, and each airman's desktop must stay totally separate from every other desktop on the server, with permissions customized for each airman. Which desktop virtualization type fits?

answers.text: Presentation virtualization on a shared Virtual Machine (VM)
answers.rationale: This type has users share one application instance on a shared server, so desktops are not separate.
Its hypervisor hosts a dedicated machine per client and enables hardware-based Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) sharing from any device.
This type decouples profiles and data from the Operating System (OS); it does not host separate desktops.
This model delivers program portions on demand to a client; it does not host separate desktops.

questions.stem: An airman works at a physical desktop in the squadron office on Monday, a virtual desktop from a deployed laptop on Wednesday, and a different physical workstation on Friday. MSgt Rush wants the airman's settings and data kept in a central data share and applied at every one of these, including the physical machines. Which approach meets this need?

answers.rationale: This type hosts dedicated Virtual Machines (VM) on a server; it does not reach the physical desktops.
This type shows a shared server application to clients; it does not manage profiles on physical desktops.
It decouples profile, settings, and data from the Operating System (OS), stores them centrally, and also works on physical desktops.
This type runs applications from central servers; it does not store a person's settings and data centrally.

questions.stem: An airman launches a large engineering program on a laptop that never had it installed. A packet capture shows only a small part of the program's code arriving at first, with more portions sent across the network when the airman opens other features. The program then runs on the laptop's own processor. Which delivery model is MSgt Rush seeing?

keywords.text: small part of the program's code

answers.rationale: This type processes nothing on the client and sends only a picture of the application.
This type runs applications on central servers and serves them up, rather than sending code portions on demand.
This type hosts a full dedicated desktop Virtual Machine (VM) on a server for each client.
Most applications need only a small portion of their code, so portions are offered across the network whenever required.

questions.stem: A flight line test set uses older industrial software that runs only on a legacy Operating System (OS). MSgt Rush must move the workstation to a current OS that receives up-to-date security patches, keep using the old software, and be able to transfer that software between computers on removable media without installing it. Which approach meets all three needs?

answers.rationale: It runs applications in foreign environments, keeps the new patched Operating System (OS), and makes them portable on removable media.
This architecture modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not make software portable on removable media.
This architecture presents emulated devices such as a switch to a guest server, not portable legacy software.
This model sends program portions across a network on demand; it does not carry software on removable media.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must run twenty small Linux web applications on one Linux server. Each application needs isolation from the others, new instances must come online extremely fast from the same base set, and no application needs its own full copy of an Operating System (OS). Which approach should MSgt Rush choose?

answers.rationale: Each of these replicates an entire Operating System (OS) for its application, so each is larger and slower to bring online.
They share one host kernel, spin up from the same base set very fast, and still isolate applications.
Each guest still runs its own modified Operating System (OS) kernel inside a Virtual Machine (VM).
This architecture presents emulated hardware to a guest server; it does not remove the guest Operating System (OS).

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans to move several web services off their Virtual Machines (VM) onto one server whose host kernel allows multiple isolated user-space instances, to gain efficiency. The services run different software stacks today. An airman asks what flexibility the squadron gives up in exchange for that efficiency. Which limitation comes with this architecture?

answers.text: The guest kernel must be modified for hyper calls
answers.rationale: Modified guest kernels that use hyper calls belong to para-virtualization, a different architecture.

answers.text: The hypervisor steals resources from its guests
answers.rationale: Resource stealing is a drawback of a hosted Type 2 hypervisor running on a busy host Operating System (OS).

answers.text: Each instance must match the host server's system
answers.rationale: This method gives greater efficiency but less flexibility: the container Operating System (OS) must match the host server's.

answers.text: Built-in device drivers limit the hardware support
answers.rationale: Limited built-in device drivers are a drawback of a bare-metal Type 1 hypervisor.

questions.stem: A training network needs a router between two subnets, but the squadron has no budget to buy, power, and maintain another physical device. MSgt Rush sets up the server so that the hypervisor presents a router to one guest virtual server, no matter what physical hardware is installed in the host. Which server virtualization architecture is this?

answers.rationale: This lets a guest reach real host hardware through hyper calls; it does not present a simulated device.
This creates isolated user-space instances on a shared kernel; it does not present a simulated router.
This pools disks from several network storage devices; it does not present a router to a guest.
The host or hypervisor emulates hardware such as a router for the guest, saving the physical device's costs.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares two Virtual Machines (VM) on one host. In the first, the guest Operating System (OS) is completely isolated and never interacts with the hypervisor. In the second, the guest kernel was modified, is not fully separate from the host, and processes faster by using host hardware directly. Which technique does the second machine use?

answers.rationale: Its modified guest kernel talks to the host through hyper calls, speeding processing by using host hardware directly.
This describes the first machine: the guest is completely isolated and does not interact with the hypervisor.
This presents emulated devices to a guest; it does not modify the guest kernel.
This uses containers on a shared host kernel, with no guest Operating System (OS) inside a Virtual Machine (VM).

questions.stem: An airman must test a software update against a copy of the base network, including several servers, a firewall, and workstations. The squadron has only one spare server, will not buy specialized servers for occasional testing, and the live network must not be touched. Which virtual environment does MSgt Rush set up for the airman?

answers.rationale: This is a copy of one Virtual Machine (VM) at a point in time, not a replica of a network.
It is a simulated lab reflecting a real network, replicating several machines on a single piece of hardware.
This separates applications on one shared kernel; it does not reflect a whole physical network.
This lets software pick the best physical server for a Virtual Machine (VM) image; it is not a test network.

questions.stem: Three Virtual Machines (VM) on separate physical hosts run the same squadron application. Monitoring shows one machine overloaded and slow to respond while the other two sit idle. MSgt Rush wants the regular workload divided so every machine carries a portion and the machines adjust dynamically to the application's demands. Which application of virtualization should MSgt Rush apply?

answers.rationale: This moves once-dedicated servers onto fewer hosts; it does not divide work among existing machines.
This lets software pick the best physical server for a Virtual Machine (VM) image, not divide regular work.
It divides the regular workload among machines on separate hardware so none sit idle and responsiveness improves.
This responds to catastrophic losses such as a whole data center, not an uneven daily workload.

questions.stem: A squadron runs twelve physical servers, each with one function such as a domain controller or a name server, and most of them sit underutilized. MSgt Rush must cut the number of machines to maintain and put existing resources to better use, so the twelve servers become Virtual Machines (VM) on one host. Which application of virtualization is this?

answers.rationale: This spreads one workload across machines on separate hardware; it does not reduce the number of servers.
This points software at a Virtual Machine (VM) image to pick a server; it does not merge servers.
This responds to catastrophic incidents such as losing a data center, not to underutilized servers.
One host now holds many once-dedicated, underutilized servers, increasing utilization and cutting maintenance costs.

questions.stem: On Monday one Virtual Machine (VM) crashed and was restarted, and on Tuesday a failed server's work shifted to another host with no outage. On Wednesday MSgt Rush writes a plan for a flood that could permanently destroy the entire base data center, relying on machine images captured in files. Which area does Wednesday's plan cover?

answers.rationale: It covers incidents far worse than a single crash or hardware failure, such as an entire data center lost.
This explains Tuesday's event, where the work shifted between machines on separate hardware.
This lets software pick a physical server for an image; it is not a plan for catastrophic loss.
This returns one machine to an earlier state, fitting a single crash rather than a lost data center.

questions.stem: An airman deletes a Virtual Machine (VM) that nobody could explain, and a squadron service goes down. MSgt Rush finds the host now holds far more machines than the squadron can manage, many of them unused, while storage, bandwidth, and electricity use keep climbing. Which problem has the squadron run into?

answers.text: A Virtual Machine (VM) patch management gap
answers.rationale: Missed patches expose security issues; they do not explain more machines than the squadron can track.
Machines created over time exceed management capacity, their functions are lost, and unused machines drain resources.
Change control governs approval of infrastructure changes; it does not describe too many machines to manage.
Load balancing divides work among machines; it does not create unmanaged, unused machines.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team patched the host and guest Operating Systems (OS), the web servers, and the database servers on schedule. A month later, an attacker gets in through a small open-source library bundled inside a third-party reporting tool on a guest. Logs captured the attack, and every change had been approved. Which area of virtualization security fell short?

answers.rationale: Every change had been approved, so the change control process worked as intended.
The logs captured the attack, so the audit trail did its job.
Updates focused on big targets while smaller third-party and open-source components were forgotten.
Nothing shows wrong host accounts or access; the attacker came in through a neglected component.

questions.stem: An airman's desktop has uncommon hardware whose drivers come only with its installed Operating System (OS). The airman must keep that OS and add a Virtual Machine (VM) that runs a different OS for a Windows-only tool, accepting some loss of VM performance. Which choice fits this desktop?

answers.rationale: This installs directly on hardware in place of the host Operating System (OS) and has limited built-in drivers.
Containers share the host kernel, so they cannot run a different Operating System (OS) than the host.
This modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not leave the installed Operating System (OS) handling drivers.
It runs on the host Operating System (OS), which handles drivers, giving better hardware compatibility but degraded performance.

questions.stem: A server runs a Type 1 hypervisor that hosts a Virtual Machine (VM) with a Linux distribution as its guest Operating System (OS). Inside that VM, MSgt Rush creates several containers that all share the Linux kernel. An airman asks how the Linux OS should be described in relation to those containers. Which term applies?

answers.rationale: The Linux guest serves as the host Operating System (OS) for containers that share its kernel.
Nothing here runs on top of the Linux system to create Virtual Machines (VM); the containers share its kernel.
The bare-metal role belongs to the Type 1 hypervisor installed on the server hardware.
Para-virtualization modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not describe the containers' shared kernel.

questions.stem: A host server runs today with only two of one component, which works but falls below the recommended amount. MSgt Rush must now place its Virtual Machines (VM) on three separate networks, keep service if one link fails, and raise speed and bandwidth. Which component should MSgt Rush add to the host?

answers.rationale: This card connects a monitor when a host lacks integrated graphics; it does not separate traffic or add redundancy.
Two can operate a host, but more are recommended for bandwidth, redundancy, speed, and separating traffic.
These raise processor efficiency for virtualization; they do not split traffic onto separate networks.
Storage limits how many machines are stored and run; it does not separate traffic or add redundancy.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush supports a forest with two domains. Each domain controller holds the objects and object attributes unique to its own domain. Airmen in the first domain now need to locate and use a shared printer published in the second domain. Which server must MSgt Rush make sure is available so that computers in one domain can find resources in the other?

keywords.text: shared printer published in the second domain

answers.rationale: A member server serves dedicated purposes such as file and print; it does not locate objects across domains.
It holds a partial replica of every object in every domain of the forest, so computers in one domain can locate resources in another.
Each domain controller holds only objects unique to its own domain, so it alone cannot locate the second domain's printer.
A domain client is a computer that uses resources; it does not let other computers locate resources in other domains.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush supports one domain whose users work at two bases. A slow Wide Area Network (WAN) link joins the two bases, and each base has its own squadrons and administrators. MSgt Rush wants every user to stay in the same domain while Active Directory (AD) reflects the slow link between the bases. Which component should MSgt Rush create for each base?

answers.rationale: Windows encourages sites when a network is divided by a slow link, and both sites can be part of the same domain.
A child domain would split the users into separate domains, but they must stay in one domain.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace; it does not reflect a slow link inside one domain.
A forest is the collection of domain trees at the top of the structure; it does not mark a slow link.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush joins a new Windows Server to the squadron's domain so that it can host the squadron's web pages. The server must belong to the domain, but it must not hold a writable copy of the domain's Active Directory (AD) information and must not authenticate logons. Which role should MSgt Rush give the new server?

answers.rationale: Every domain controller holds a complete, writable copy of the domain's directory information and authenticates users.
A global catalog server is normally a domain controller and stores replicas of directory objects.
A domain client runs a user's desktop environment to reach resources; it does not host web pages for the squadron.
It belongs to a domain without being the domain controller and is used for dedicated purposes such as web servers.

questions.stem: A small base runs one domain with a single domain controller, plus a member server for file and print services. When the domain controller fails, no airman can log on to the domain, though the file server keeps running. MSgt Rush wants the next failure of one server to leave domain logons working. Which addition does MSgt Rush need?

keywords.text: no airman can log on to the domain

answers.rationale: A member server is not a domain controller, so it cannot authenticate users when the only one fails.
A site maps the physical structure of the network; adding one does not add a server that authenticates users.
Networks normally have more than one, so if one fails others store the directory structure and authenticate users.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace; it adds no backup for this domain's logons.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush changes the replication topology data on a domain controller in AF.Domain. Later, MSgt Rush signs on to a domain controller in Medical.Domain, a different domain in the same forest, and finds the same change there. Which directory partition holds the data that MSgt Rush changed?

answers.rationale: It contains replication topology data replicated throughout the forest, and every domain controller in the forest has a replica.
The domain partition stores users, computers, and groups for one specific domain, not data shared by another domain.
The schema partition stores class and attribute definitions for objects, not replication topology data.
The forest root domain is the first domain created in the forest; it is not a directory partition.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must add a badge number to the types of information that a user account object can hold. The change has to reach every user object in the forest, existing and future, not only the users of one domain or one Organizational Unit (OU). Which part of Active Directory (AD) defines this for the user object type?

answers.rationale: The configuration partition stores configuration objects and replication topology, not the definition of a user object type.
Each type of object is defined through it, the template of attributes that sets the types of information an object can hold.
The domain partition stores the users and other objects of one domain, not the definitions of object types.
An Organizational Unit (OU) holds users, groups, and computers; it does not define what a user object can hold.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush creates user accounts for two airmen in one Organizational Unit (OU). Both accounts are user objects of the same type, and Active Directory (AD) keeps them as two separate entities. MSgt Rush reviews their attributes to see how AD distinguishes the two objects. Which statement describes what MSgt Rush finds?

keywords.text: user objects of the same type

answers.rationale: All objects of the same type or class have the same set of attributes.
Objects of the same class are distinguished from each other by having different values for at least one attribute.
Syntaxes belong to the schema for the object type, and both objects share that same type.
Some attributes, such as First Name for a user object, are required to have values.

questions.stem: In an Organizational Unit (OU), MSgt Rush finds a printer object and several user objects. MSgt Rush tries to move one of the user objects into the printer object, but Active Directory (AD) does not allow it, although moving the same user object into another OU works. Which description fits the printer object?

keywords.text: move one of the user objects into the printer object

answers.rationale: A container object can hold other objects, but the printer object could not hold the user object.
A child domain is a domain created after the root, and domains are container objects that hold other objects.
It is found in containers such as Organizational Units (OUs) and cannot contain other directory objects.
The forest root is the first domain created in the forest, and domains can hold other objects.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is deploying a new Active Directory (AD) forest for a base. The plan calls for one domain used only to administer the forest and three regional domains for the squadrons, each with its own Organizational Units (OUs). Before building any of the regional domains, which domain must MSgt Rush already have created?

keywords.text: building any of the regional domains

answers.rationale: It must be created before any of the regional domains and provides the foundation for the infrastructure.
Child domains are created after the root, so a regional child domain cannot come before it.
A domain tree is a collection of domains, not a single domain that must exist before the regional ones.
Squadron domains are regional domains, and none of those may be built ahead of the foundation domain.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush manages two domain trees, AF.Domain and Medical.Domain, that share one global catalog and one directory schema. Each domain in them has its own security policies and its own security boundary. MSgt Rush must name the outermost boundary of the directory service, within which the users and computers of both trees are accessible. Which structure is it?

keywords.text: outermost boundary of the directory service

answers.rationale: Each domain is a security boundary for its own objects, but it does not hold both trees.
A site maps the physical structure of the network and is defined by subnets, not a security boundary.
A domain tree holds domains sharing one namespace, and the two trees here have different namespaces.
It represents the security boundary within which users, computers, and groups are accessible and is the outermost boundary.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans a third Domain Name System (DNS) server for a branch site. The site's two existing name servers will keep sending it updates, but the new server will hold no zone of its own, and its answers must never count as authoritative for the zone. Which name server role fits the new server?

answers.rationale: It holds no zone, is authoritative for no zone, and receives updates from primary and secondary servers.
This server holds a zone copy and can answer authoritatively for its zone.
This server holds the master zone file and is authoritative for its zone.
These servers form the upper-most layer of the namespace, not a branch site role.

questions.stem: The primary name server for a zone at MSgt Rush's site goes offline for repairs. Clients must still get authoritative answers for that zone from another server at the site that holds its own copy of the zone, received from the primary before the outage. Which server at the site can give those answers?

answers.rationale: This server keeps copies of zone information but is not authoritative for any zone.
It obtains its zone files from the primary and is authoritative, so it can answer queries for its zone.
These servers sit at the top of the namespace and do not hold the site's zone.
These servers resolve names such as .com and do not hold the site's zone.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must change the Mail Exchanger (MX) record for a zone that three name servers at the site handle. Each server answers lookups for the zone, and the change must reach all of them through the normal replication between servers, not by editing each one in turn. On which server must MSgt Rush enter the change?

answers.rationale: Its zone copies are read only and come from another server by zone transfer.
This server holds no zone information and only receives updates from other servers.
It holds the master copy of the zone file and passes zone information to the other servers.
These servers form the top layer of the namespace and do not hold the site's zone.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush updates an Address (A) record on the primary name server. At a second site, the secondary name server still holds its read-only text copy of the zone without the update, and an airman there cannot edit that copy. Which process must run before the secondary's copy of the zone includes the new record?

answers.rationale: Expiry removes cached entries from a local server; it does not update a zone copy.
The secondary zone database can only be updated by the primary server through this process.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush moves a web server to a new Internet Protocol (IP) address and updates its Address (A) record on the primary name server. An airman's local name server had answered a lookup for that site shortly before, and the airman keeps reaching the old address. Which setting decides how long the local name server keeps giving that stored answer?

answers.rationale: This parameter defines how long an entry remains cached on the local name server.
This record holds admin details for the zone, not how long a cached answer lasts.
Zone transfers synchronize primary and secondary zones, not cached answers on a local server.
This record identifies servers to contact for a domain, not how long answers stay cached.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches the local Domain Name System (DNS) server resolve rhope-ops.github.io for an airman. The root server returns only the name of the .io server, and the local server then sends its own request to that .io server. The .io server returns the name of the github.io server, and again the local server asks that server directly. Which query type is MSgt Rush watching?

answers.rationale: In this type each server passes the request on to the next server down.
The local server keeps responsibility and asks each server in the hierarchy itself.
This lookup resolves an address to a name, but the airman asked for a name.

questions.stem: An airman's client asks the local Domain Name System (DNS) server for rhope-ops.github.io. The local server sends the request to the root server, the root server sends it on to the .io server, and that server sends it on to the github.io server. The reply then travels back through each server in reverse order to the client. Which query type did the client start?

answers.rationale: In this type the local server asks each server itself instead of each server passing it on.
Each server takes responsibility and delegates the request to the next server down.
This lookup resolves an address to a name, but the client asked for a name.

questions.stem: A new Domain Name System (DNS) server at MSgt Rush's site already resolves every hostname to its Internet Protocol (IP) address for clients, and name service works without problems. MSgt Rush now sets up authentication of email traffic sources, which needs a zone type that normal operation does not require. Which zone type must MSgt Rush add?

answers.rationale: The server already resolves hostnames to addresses, so this zone type is in place.
This read-only copy of a primary zone does not add a new lookup direction.
This master zone file already supports the server's hostname lookups.
This zone type is not required for operation but is required to authenticate email traffic sources.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush builds a new Domain Name System (DNS) server whose only zone so far answers requests that give an Internet Protocol (IP) address and ask for the hostname. The server does not function properly yet. Which zone type must the server have at least one of before it can function properly?

answers.rationale: The server must have at least one forward lookup database to function properly.
The server already has this zone type, and it is not required for operation.
This read-only copy comes from a primary zone and is not the required database.
Cached entries expire and are not a zone database the server requires.

questions.stem: Two Domain Name System (DNS) servers at MSgt Rush's site keep the same zone as text files. On the first server, an airman can open the file and change a record. On the second server, the file can be updated only by the first server through a synchronization process. Which database is stored on the first server?

answers.rationale: This read-only copy matches the second server, which only the primary can update.
It is the master copy of the zone database file, stored as a standard text file.
Cached entries are kept for a limited time and are not an editable zone file.
The root zone belongs to the upper-most layer of the namespace, not this site.

questions.stem: During an iterative query for rhope-ops.github.io, the local name server first gets a referral from the root server and then a referral from the .io server. The local name server then asks a third server, and that server replies with the Internet Protocol (IP) address for rhope-ops.github.io, ending the search. Which kind of server sent that final reply?

answers.rationale: This server sent the first referral and did not know the address.
This server sent the second referral and did not know the address.
The iterative query continues until it reaches the server that holds the address for the hostname.
This server is not authoritative for any zone and was not part of the search.

questions.stem: Airmen at MSgt Rush's site reach the domain's web server by name without trouble, but email sent to addresses in the domain is never handed to the host that forwards the domain's messages. MSgt Rush suspects a missing resource record in the zone. Which record type identifies that forwarding host for the domain?

answers.rationale: This record creates an alias for a host name, not a forwarding host.
This record maps a host name to an address and already works for the web server.
This record identifies name servers to contact for the domain.
This record indicates the mail forwarder host for the domain.

questions.stem: One web host at MSgt Rush's site is already mapped to its Internet Protocol (IP) address. Airmen should also be able to reach that same host by a second, shorter name, and MSgt Rush wants that name to point to the existing host name, not to a second address entry. Which resource record type does MSgt Rush add?

answers.rationale: This record creates an alias for a host name.
This record maps a name to an address, which MSgt Rush wants to avoid adding.
This record describes the host's Operating System (OS) and processor, not a second name.
This record identifies name servers for the domain, not a second host name.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares a zone on the primary name server and on a secondary name server to check whether the two are in step. MSgt Rush looks for the one record that carries the zone's serial number together with the admin email contact for that domain. Which resource record type holds those details?

answers.rationale: This record identifies which servers to contact when looking for a domain.
It contains admin details such as email, serial number, and zone sync for the domain.
This record describes a host's Operating System (OS) and processor type.

A wanted tool that works as expected while hidden extra code opens a back door for a hacker fits this program.
A rootkit is installed on a system by a hacker, but here she downloaded the tool herself.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds that hidden code copied itself from machine to machine through a vulnerable network port overnight. Every workstation had stayed powered on since the previous day and sat idle at the logon screen. By morning the network is clogged, and its only traffic is copies of the code. Which kind of program is it?

answers.rationale: A computer virus relies on human activity such as running a program to spread, but every workstation sat idle at the logon screen.
A boot-sector virus runs when a computer is booted, but these workstations had stayed powered on since the previous day.
Spyware sends user information to a remote system, but the only traffic here is copies of the code.
Copying itself through a vulnerable port with no user action at all marks this self-replicating program.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush notices that a workstation's browser now opens an unfamiliar home page and its network link has slowed. Hidden software that the administrator's tools miss is running on it. The airman at that workstation opens and edits every file as usual and sees only his usual work windows. Which kind of program is it?

answers.rationale: Hidden software that redirects the browser and slows the network link fits this program, which collects information for a hacker.
Adware loads advertisements, typically in pop-up windows, but the airman sees only his usual work windows.
Ransomware locks the screen or encrypts files for a ransom, but the airman opens and edits every file as usual.
A rootkit gives a hacker hidden privileged access, while a redirected browser and slowed network link point to software that collects user information.

questions.stem: A unit wants one device placed between its workstations and the Internet to handle the requests people send as they browse sites. It should give people privacy, block banned sites, and work as one part of the unit's larger barrier that restricts traffic to and from the network. Which device fits?

keywords.text: between its workstations and the Internet

answers.rationale: A firewall is the larger barrier that restricts traffic, while this device works as one part of it.
A device between workstations and the Internet that gives security, privacy and site blocking, often within a firewall, fits here.
A mail gateway sends and receives email for the organization, while this device handles the requests people send as they browse sites.
Anti-spyware is protective software against spyware, not one device placed between workstations and the Internet.

questions.stem: An outside cleaning company is hired to mop floors and empty trash in a base office, and its crew gets badges that open the server room. One crew member carelessly props that door open, and files are exposed. Every base record stays on the base's own machines in that room. Which supply chain vulnerability does the company represent?

answers.rationale: Third party data storage concerns an outside provider handling records off-site, but every record stays on the base's own machines.
Compromised hardware or software comes from a vendor's products, but this company is hired only to mop floors and empty trash.
Supply management covers enterprise functions such as sourcing and vendor management, not one hired company's careless crew.
A hired company supporting the base, whose granted physical entry is left open through carelessness, fits this vulnerability.

questions.stem: Each week an airman runs a tool from her workstation that sends test traffic over the network to every base host. Its report names the hosts that are missing fixes and could be attacked next. Another team then installs those fixes. Which mitigation is she running?

answers.rationale: A weekly run that identifies hosts open to attack, so that another team can fix them, fits this mitigation.
Software patching repairs a flaw, but here another team installs the fixes after the tool's report.
Anti-virus inspects the contents of each file on a system, while this tool sends test traffic over the network to every host.
Monitoring logs looks for signs of a compromise that has already happened, while this report names hosts that could be attacked next.

questions.stem: A hacker group outside the base posts that it may try to break into the base mail servers through an unpatched mail program. That week the mail servers run normally and every log is clean. An airman logs the unpatched program as one item on her list and the group's possible move as another. Which term names that second item?

answers.rationale: A vulnerability is the flaw itself, which she logged as the first item, not the group's possible move.
A possible danger that may exploit the unpatched program, before anyone acts, is the second item.
A network attack is an intentional act against a system, but the servers run normally and every log is clean.
An inside attack starts within the security perimeter, but this group is outside the base.

questions.stem: A base web host suddenly receives far more page requests than it can answer, and legitimate users are blocked. Every request traces back to one computer outside the base and asks only for the public home page. Every page on the host stays intact. Which attack is this?

answers.rationale: That form involves multiple computers, usually a botnet, but every request traces back to one computer.
Unauthorized access aims to reach a resource the host should not provide, but every request asks only for the public home page.
One machine sending more requests than the host can handle, so legitimate users are blocked, fits this attack.
Data destruction makes stored files unreadable, but every page on the host stays intact.

questions.stem: Thousands of home computers have been compromised, and their hidden software lets hackers send them commands through a chat room. On command they flood a base site with requests. On other days they collect stolen information and send spam. Which term names these computers as a group?

answers.rationale: Compromised computers turned into robots that hackers activate through chat rooms to attack, collect stolen information and spam form this group.
That attack is one thing these computers do on command, but they also collect stolen information and send spam.
A worm self-replicates without any commands, but hackers send these computers commands through a chat room.
A rootkit is hidden software on one system, not thousands of compromised computers acting together.

questions.stem: A new airman's account, set up properly by the unit, lets her read email and use the share drives. When she tries to install a program missing from the unit's approved list, the system refuses. Only the unit's system staff change the hardware and firmware settings that run the system. Which classification does her account hold?

answers.rationale: Administrator access gives full control of hardware, software and firmware operations, which only the system staff hold here.
Unauthorized access reaches a resource a machine should not provide, but her account was set up properly.
Selected control over email and share drives, limited to what the unit approves, fits this classification.
Elevation of privilege lets someone do what they are not authorized to do, but the system refused her install.

questions.stem: An airman learns that a program on her workstation, which arrived in an email attachment, was written by its maker on purpose to wreck files. It stays as one copy on her workstation, and its only visible effect is a folder of wrecked files. Which term best names this program?

answers.rationale: A program built on purpose to damage a system, which reached her through email, is named by its maker's intent.
Defective software has a legitimate purpose with harmful bugs, but this maker wrote it on purpose to wreck files.
Adware automatically loads advertisements on the screen, but this program's only visible effect is a folder of wrecked files.
A computer virus exists to reproduce itself as often as possible, but this program stays as one copy.

questions.stem: Hidden code arrived on an airman's workstation inside a program she ran from a shared flash drive, and it now copies itself into other programs as often as it can. It spreads only when people run or share infected files. Warnings and error messages now appear on her screen at unusual times. Which kind of harmful code is it?

answers.rationale: A worm self-replicates without user action, but this code spreads only when people run or share infected files.
Code hiding in programs that reproduces as often as it can and spreads through human activity fits this kind.
A Trojan horse opens a back door for a hacker, while this code copies itself into other programs as often as it can.
Spyware sends collected information to a remote system, while warnings and errors at unusual times are a symptom of self-reproducing code.

questions.stem: When an airman's visiting laptop tries to join the base's wired or wireless system, small software is installed on it and scans it once for current virus definitions. The laptop is let on as soon as that scan passes. By the time she unplugs it that evening, it holds only the programs she brought. Which option is the base using?

keywords.text: let on as soon as that scan passes
it holds only the programs she brought

answers.rationale: Permanent agents stay installed to keep monitoring the laptop, but by evening it holds only the programs she brought.
Software installed when the laptop tries to join, used for one compliance scan and gone by the time she unplugs, is this temporary kind.
Agentless checks are done by the authentication server with no software placed on the client, but here small software is installed on the laptop.
802.1X lets a client on only after it provides valid credentials, but this laptop is let on as soon as its scan passes.

questions.stem: An airman types his username, and the server finds it in its user list. He then enters a password he mistyped, the server compares it with the stored one, and he is turned away before any folder or task is offered; the server logs the failed attempt's time. Which step did the airman fail?

keywords.text: compares it with the stored one

answers.rationale: Identification is the username claim, and the server found that username in its user list.
Authorization grants permitted tasks only after the account is verified, and he was turned away before any were offered.
Accounting logs usage such as the failed attempt's time; it is not the password comparison that he failed.
The mistyped password did not match the stored one, so he failed the check that he is who he claims to be.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team now manages one set of credentials per user for the whole base. An attacker who stole just his password typed it once and then moved among the mail, file and training servers. His laptop had passed the switch's credential check before it joined the base wired system. Which setup explains the attacker's reach?

answers.rationale: This checks credentials before the laptop joins the wired system; it does not carry one logon on to the mail, file and training servers.
Multifactor authentication would also demand something he has, such as a token, but the attacker got in with just the password.
One logon that opens several systems without more credentials, managed as one set per user, lets one stolen password reach every server.
Separate logons would make the attacker sign in at each server, but he typed the password once.

questions.stem: An airman plugs his laptop into a wall port, and the switch holds back all traffic until he types a username and password. A server behind the switch does all the checking. When he mistypes the password, the port stays shut; with the right one, it opens at once. Which protection is the switch enforcing?

keywords.text: holds back all traffic until he types a username and password
When he mistypes the password, the port stays shut

answers.rationale: Host health checks judge a system's updates and antivirus software, but here the port opens or stays shut on the typed password.
Terms of usage apply to users joining a wireless network, but this laptop is plugged into a wall port.
A wired switch that allows the connection only after a server behind it approves the typed credentials enforces this protocol.
Agent-based checks rely on software installed on the client, but here the server behind the switch does all the checking.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush connects to the base's virtual private network, and one central server checks his password against its user database before letting him on. The same server then opens only the folders his role permits and records his session's access time and bandwidth. Which kind of service is this?

keywords.text: opens only the folders his role permits

answers.rationale: One central server that checks his password, opens only permitted folders and records his usage provides all three services together.
Checking the password and opening permitted folders are only two parts; recording access time and bandwidth is the third.
This sets conditions a system must meet before it joins the network, while this server also opens only the folders his role permits.
This detects and logs suspicious activity, while this server checks his password against its user database.

questions.stem: An airman inserts his smartcard, and the logon screen shows his name and asks for his password. He is called away before typing it, and his mail and shared folders stay locked behind the logon screen. The reader notes the time the card went in, and the password box is still empty when he returns. Which step has the airman completed?

answers.rationale: Presenting the smartcard tells the system who he claims to be, and that is all he finished.
Authentication would need him to type the password for the server to check, and he was called away before typing it.
Authorization grants permitted tasks only after the account is verified, and his mail and folders stayed locked behind the logon screen.
Accounting logs the resources a user consumes during a session, and he is still at the empty password box with no session started.

questions.stem: Weeks after airmen log on to the base wireless system, a report lists every session with its account, date, time and source. Routine sessions fill most of its pages. An airman reads it to see how long each squadron stayed on the system. Which part of the centralized logon service kept these records?

keywords.text: lists every session with its account, date, time and source
how long each squadron stayed on the system

answers.rationale: This shows date, time, source and account in notifications about suspicious activity on one host, but this report is mostly routine sessions.
Authentication checks what users enter at logon, while this report is a record of every session kept afterward.
Authorization grants access and permitted tasks, while this report shows how long each squadron stayed on.
Logging every session with its account and how long each squadron stayed on records the access time users consume.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team has finished writing the code for a scheduling application and is now finding and fixing its crashes and other bugs. The application runs only on the developers' own computers, and every bug report so far comes from the developers themselves. Which part of the build process is the team in?

keywords.text: runs only on the developers' own computers

answers.rationale: Implementation is when the code gets written, and the team has already finished writing it.
Deployment installs the application on the production servers, but it still runs only on the developers' own computers.
Checking finished code for crashes and bugs before it is installed for users is the functionality check that comes next.
Maintenance fixes problems that users report in feedback, but every bug report so far comes from the developers.

questions.stem: A website builds each page with commands that run on a shared lab computer, keeps an airman logged on between visits and remembers his page layout. Later another airman sits down at that computer and obtains the first airman's logon details. Which weakness did the second airman use?

keywords.text: keeps an airman logged on between visits

answers.rationale: The site stored his preferences and logon information on that shared computer, where the next person at it could see them.
This injects malicious code into a website to steal session data, while here the second airman took the details at the same computer.
These can manipulate a system with full access, while what this site kept on the computer was his page layout and logon.
Scripts can build pages and modify a system, while what the second airman used was the logon kept between visits.

questions.stem: A website the airman visits leaves an item on his workstation, made to automate a nightly cleanup of old files. Each night at 0200, while the office is empty, the item runs and changes the system's settings. Which weakness is at work?

keywords.text: made to automate a nightly cleanup of old files

answers.rationale: Cookies hold preferences and logon information, while this item runs and changes the system's settings.
Commands carried out by a program to automate a process, changing the system with no user input, are this weakness.
ActiveX controls can manipulate a system, but changes made with no user input while the office is empty mark scripts.
This attack injects code into a website to compromise user accounts, while this item automates a nightly cleanup on the workstation.

questions.stem: One tool watches every packet reaching a file server on the base around the clock. It decides which logon attempts look suspicious, logs each one and emails an alert to an airman, who then reviews her inbox. Which choice names the whole tool?

keywords.text: decides which logon attempts look suspicious
emails an alert to an airman

answers.rationale: A tool that spots suspicious activity, logs it and alerts an administrator matches every stated fact.
A prevention tool takes corrective action against what it finds, while this tool logs each attempt and emails an alert.
A sensor only collects traffic and forwards it; it does not decide which attempts look suspicious.
The analysis engine judges packets, while logging each attempt belongs to the whole tool.

questions.stem: On one workstation, a tool spots suspicious activity on that workstation alone and shows notifications in its own application window, also emailing copies to an airman. He reviews each event's date, time, source and account to decide whether a configuration change is needed. Which choice names this tool?

keywords.text: decide whether a configuration change is needed

answers.rationale: This analyzes traffic across the network for multiple systems, but this tool watches one workstation alone.
Watching one workstation and showing notifications that an airman reviews to decide on a configuration change fits every stated fact.
This also runs on one host but stops attacks itself, while this tool gives an airman events to review for a configuration change.
A console receives alerts that another component found; it does not spot suspicious activity itself.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must watch all traffic crossing the base's segments for activity on many servers at once. He installs one product as its own device; it analyzes the packets and logs the details of anything suspicious, then sends him an alert for each one. Which product did he install?

keywords.text: sends him an alert for each one

answers.rationale: A host-based tool watches only its own host, but he must watch activity on many servers at once.
A prevention tool takes corrective action against attacks, while this product logs details and sends him an alert.
One device that analyzes all traffic across the segments for many servers, then logs details and sends alerts, matches every fact.
The analysis engine only judges the packets it receives; logging details belongs to the whole product.

questions.stem: An airman must add new reports to a folder on a Windows server, delete old ones and decide which other airmen may open it. What she is given must hold even when she signs on at the server itself, not only across the network. Which choice fits?

keywords.text: decide which other airmen may open it

answers.rationale: Modify lets her add and delete reports, but it gives no way to decide which other airmen may open the folder.
Write lets her add new reports, but deleting old ones needs a broader permission such as Modify.
Only the permission that gives every possible right lets her add, delete and change who may open the folder, at the server or remotely.
A share permission applies when the folder is reached across the network, so it would not hold when she signs on at the server.

questions.stem: An airman must keep a folder on a server's drive closed to everyone but her flight, even when they sit at that server rather than reach it across the network. The drive now uses FAT32, and she must not erase its data. What must the drive have before she can begin?

keywords.text: closed to everyone but her flight

answers.rationale: FAT32 keeps her data untouched, but this legacy format has no permissions to keep the folder closed to everyone but her flight.
The drive must first carry the Windows format that adds permissions, and a drive in another format can be converted to it.
Share permissions apply when the folder is published to the network, so they do not cover her flight sitting at that server.
The access list is what she builds once the drive is ready, not something the drive must have before she can begin.

questions.stem: An airman installed an agent on his computer and set it so every web page he asks for goes first to one box on the base network, not straight to the router. The box fetches the page from the Internet and keeps a copy so the next airman gets it faster. Which choice names that box?

answers.rationale: A reverse proxy takes requests from systems on the Internet for internal servers, but this box fetches pages from the Internet for him.
A transparent proxy needs no software or setup on the user's computer, yet this airman installed an agent and set it up.
A packet-filtering firewall only blocks or allows packets by address and port; it does not keep page copies for the next airman.
An inside client sends each request to a box that fetches the page from the Internet, returns it and caches it.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush adds rules to a Cisco router so that packets from one workstation to the mail server are dropped while its web traffic to the same server still passes. He gives the rule set the number 120 and applies it to an interface. Which choice is he building?

answers.rationale: A standard access list is numbered 1 to 99 and filters only by source address, so the number 120 rules it out.
Router rules numbered 100 and above that filter by destination and protocol, then applied to an interface, form this kind of list.
A software-based firewall protects only the one system it is installed on, but these rules are added to a Cisco router.
Implicit deny drops packets that no rule allows, but here web traffic to the same server is meant to pass.

questions.stem: An airman adds an entry to a Group Policy Object (GPO) so that every workstation in the domain, whoever signs on, gets the same detailed inbound and outbound traffic rules. Which choice is he configuring?

keywords.text: detailed inbound and outbound traffic rules

answers.rationale: Advanced settings set detailed inbound and outbound rules inside the firewall itself, not through an entry pushed to the whole domain.
Software Restriction Policies control what software may run, not inbound and outbound traffic rules.
User settings follow a person to any machine, but these rules must apply to each workstation whoever signs on.
This Security Settings entry under computer settings configures the built-in traffic filter, so every workstation gets the same rules.

questions.stem: An airman must make every workstation in a training room lock an account after three wrong passwords and refuse to run a game program. These limits are tied to the workstations themselves and apply to every person who signs on at one of them. Which choice covers every one of these needs?

answers.rationale: Account lockout and limits on which software runs both belong to the category that stays with the system whoever signs on.
User settings follow a person to any machine, but these limits are tied to the training room workstations themselves.
Account Policies set lockout and password rules but not which software may run, so the game would still start.
Software Restriction Policies stop the game from running but do not lock an account after wrong passwords.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants limits on the traffic that leaves his one laptop. He lets one program through, asks to be told when a program is blocked, and turns the protection off only for one network location. Which choice is he using?

keywords.text: told when a program is blocked

answers.rationale: A hardware-based firewall sits at the edge of a network, but these limits are set on his one laptop.
Iptables controls outgoing traffic, but being told when a program is blocked is a notification setting of a different firewall.
Letting a program through, notification settings and turning protection off per network location are features of the firewall included with his laptop's platform.
A proxy server limits which web sites can be visited, not which programs are let through on one laptop.

questions.stem: An airman's firewall plan splits a base's systems into a part for staff computers, a part between two firewalls for the web server, and a part for visiting laptops. Every connection from one part to another must pass a firewall rule. Which term covers all three parts together?

answers.rationale: The area between two firewalls covers only the web server's part, not the staff computers' part.
The intranet zone is only the staff computers' part; a part for visiting laptops is a guest zone, not the intranet.
Each part that the firewalls split off for protection, from the staff computers to the visiting laptops, is named by this term.
Additional zones, such as a guest zone, add to the main ones, but the part between two firewalls is one of the main ones.

questions.stem: An airman and the unit that owns the mission study data copied from the affected base servers to learn how the attacker got in, why the defenses failed and what the attack could mean for the mission. What they learn tells them which further data to request and will help the unit plan a course of action to prevent a repeat. Which phase is she in?

answers.rationale: Post-incident analysis is the final postmortem review, while their findings still steer which further data to request.
Preliminary analysis and identification is done by operations centers that categorize the activity, while this work includes the mission's owning unit.
Studying how the attacker got in and the possible mission effect, with the mission's owning unit, to guide further data requests is this phase.
Response and recovery restores systems and prevents further damage, while these two weigh what the attack could mean for the mission.

questions.stem: When a virus appears on a workstation, an airman of the response staff logs the time and unplugs its network cable to contain the spread. He then activates the rest of the staff and leaves sizing up the full scale of the problem to another member. Which role does he hold?

keywords.text: activates the rest of the staff

answers.rationale: Containing the virus by unplugging the cable and then activating the rest of the staff is this member's primary goal.
The Team Leader makes sure members know their roles, but unplugging a cable to contain the spread is not that job.
A Technical Specialist sizes up the scale of a problem, but this airman leaves that to another member.
A Documentation Specialist logs each problem, but this airman also activates the rest of the staff, which is not that job.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must prepare his squadron to handle security breaches. His first step will fix and record each breach in a timely manner and draws on different skill sets, such as knowing Linux servers. Only after that does he write down the breach types and each person's job, and later he schedules practice drills. What did he put in place first?

answers.rationale: An incident response plan names breach types and each person's job, but he writes it only after that first step.
A Technical Specialist knows one area such as Linux servers, but this first step draws on different skill sets.
A group with varied skills that fixes and records breaches is the first thing an organization puts in place to prepare.
Exercise planning schedules practice drills, and he does that later, not first.

questions.stem: Before any breach has occurred and once the squadron's breach-handling staff are in place, MSgt Rush writes one document for the whole organization. It names the kinds of breaches to expect, gives each member a job, and sets when practice drills will run. Which document has he written?

answers.rationale: That plan details the actions and responsible people for restoring systems after a breach, but no breach has occurred yet.
A document every organization creates once its staff are in place, naming breach types and each member's job, is this one.
That team is the staff group itself, already in place, not the one document he writes.
Exercise planning only sets practice drills, but this document also names the kinds of breaches to expect.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reads one section of his unit's breach-handling document so that the staff know what to do. It says the Technical Specialist checks the servers ahead of any breach, corrects the problem while one is under way and helps explain the cause once it is over. It then sets out the same three stages for the Documentation Specialist and the Legal Advisor. Which section is he reading?

answers.rationale: Exercise planning sets up practice of breach events, while this section gives each member's tasks while a real breach is under way.
User roles names the first responder, while this section sets out tasks for the Documentation Specialist and Legal Advisor too.
The Team Leader is a team member who makes sure others know their part, while he is reading a section of a document.
A section giving each member's job before, during and after a breach is the one he is reading.

questions.stem: Before any breach occurred, MSgt Rush wrote one section of his unit's breach-handling document for users, not for the analysis staff. An airman who spots a strange pop-up uses it to learn when and how to speak up, who the person to alert first is, and what elements the write-up must contain. Which section did he write?

keywords.text: when and how to speak up

answers.rationale: User roles names the member to be notified first, but this section also tells users when and how to speak up.
Determining reporting requirements is an analysis step taken within an hour of a breach, but this section was written before any breach.
A plan section telling users when and how to raise a possible breach, whom to alert and what to include is this one.
Incident categories name the types of breaches, but this section tells users what elements the write-up must contain.

questions.stem: A postmortem of a malware breach records its lessons learned and traces the spread to how slowly the staff carried out the unit's chosen steps for isolating infected servers. The results go to the affected unit for correction. The unit will work out why those chosen steps failed and then rewrite them. What will the unit revise?

keywords.text: how slowly the staff carried out

answers.rationale: Missing policies and procedures are a postmortem finding, while this postmortem traces the spread to slowly carried-out isolation steps.
The unit's chosen steps for isolating servers are its planned responses, which postmortem results lead the unit to revise.
Lessons learned are what the postmortem records, while the correction falls on the slowly performed isolation steps.
Inadequate infrastructure defenses are a postmortem finding, while the unit here must work out why its chosen isolation steps failed.

questions.stem: Each night, an airman's job copies to tape only the files whose archive bit reads 1, so each changed file gets a second copy. Afterward, each copied file's bit reads 0, and she keeps every nightly tape. Which choice names the nightly job?

answers.rationale: Copying only files whose bit reads 1 and then clearing each bit matches this nightly job, the type normally used daily.
A full job copies every file without relying on the archive bit, but this job copies only files whose bit reads 1.
Mirroring reflects data onto a second drive as it is saved, but this job copies to tape each night.
A differential job does not clear the archive bit, but here each copied file's bit reads 0 afterward.

questions.stem: Before loading a new computer image, an airman runs a tape job that takes far longer than his nightly jobs and copies even files whose archive bit already reads 0. Afterward, every copied file's bit reads 0. Which choice names this job?

answers.rationale: An incremental job copies only data changed since the previous job, but this one copies even files whose bit already reads 0.
Copying every file whatever its bit and then clearing each bit matches this long job, a safe step before major changes.
A differential job does not clear the archive bit, yet every copied file's bit reads 0 after this job.
Mirroring keeps a duplicate on a second drive as data is saved, not on a tape set made before a new image.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is building an authentication server with two drives. Every file saved to one drive must also appear on the other, and if either drive fails, the server must carry on with all its data from the drive that is left. Which choice names what he needs?

answers.rationale: Level 0 works with two drives but has no redundancy, so one failed drive would lose all the data.
Parity rebuilds lost data from an index and needs at least three disks, rather than copying each file to the other drive.
Two drives that each hold every saved file give a built-in backup, a setup commonly used for authentication servers.
Level 1+0 also mirrors data, but it needs four disks and suits application servers, while this authentication server has two drives.

questions.stem: An airman joins two drives in the unit's voice and video streaming server so that the server reads and writes faster for its viewers. Everything the setup writes to the two drives is file data. Which method is she using?

answers.rationale: Mirroring gives a built-in backup and is commonly used for authentication servers, while this is a voice and video streaming server.
Parity adds an index used to rebuild lost data, but everything this setup writes is file data.
Double parity uses two parity bits and needs at least four disks, while this server joins only two drives.
Dividing data between two drives, with no copy and no parity, boosts performance and suits voice and video streaming.

questions.stem: Bad code pushed to a base web service causes an outage, and MSgt Rush returns the software to the state that worked before the change by running one script. He works alone at his desk from the records of every tracked change, and the script undoes the bad code. Which term names what the tracked changes gave him?

answers.rationale: Tracked changes let him roll back to the last state that worked, the first benefit configuration management gives.
Site reliability refers to how often the service is up, while he returned the software to its state before the change.
Scalability lets servers be added by running a script, but his script undid the bad code using the tracked changes.
A recovery plan calls up a team and follows written step-by-step instructions, while he worked alone from tracked change records.

questions.stem: A unit writes a document that lists its servers, laptops, software applications and data, and says where its backup tapes are stored. The same document gives step-by-step instructions for restoring systems and data after a loss. Which document is the unit writing?

answers.rationale: Data backup policies set backup frequency, type and storage location, but they do not list every server, laptop and application.
Configuration management tracks hardware and software changes, but it does not say where backup tapes are stored.
An inventory of hardware, software and data, backup storage details and step-by-step instructions all belong in this document.
Backup and recovery is the process of copying and restoring data, not a document a unit writes.

questions.stem: A shopping website that MSgt Rush uses is compromised, and the characters he typed to sign in there are stolen. Within a day, attackers also get into his email and bank accounts. What he typed ran to 24 characters, was made up at random and opened with K7#q. Which guideline did he skip?

answers.rationale: Length helps against cracking, and 24 characters is already past the 18-character minimum.
A mix of characters makes cracking harder, and an opening of K7#q already mixes a capital, a number, a symbol and a lower-case letter.
Dictionary words are easy to crack, but characters made up at random form no dictionary word.
One stolen secret opened his email and bank as well, so he had reused it on several services.

questions.stem: A wing tracks every software and hardware modification on its servers in a log, pushes new settings centrally to each group of servers and flags outdated and noncompliant settings. Its records also let the airman on duty put back the most recent working settings after a failed patch. Which choice names what the wing is doing?

answers.rationale: Tracking every modification, pushing settings centrally to groups and restoring working settings from records are tools of this process.
A baseline configuration is a starting point that records how a system should be set up; it does not push settings centrally.
Provisioning adds more resources, usually servers, to running applications, while flagging outdated and noncompliant settings belongs to a different process.
Putting back working settings is only one benefit, while the wing also tracks every modification and pushes settings to groups.

questions.stem: One hard drive in the only server of an airman's office fails during the duty day. Users keep opening and saving their files in that same minute. The broken drive is swapped out the next week. Which measure kept the files ready?

keywords.text: Users keep opening and saving their files in that same minute

answers.rationale: Drives working together inside the one server supplied the missing data, so the files stayed ready in the same minute the drive failed.
Clustering has a second server take over the workload, but this office has only one server.
Backups restore corrupt or unavailable data afterward, but users kept opening their files in the same minute the drive failed.
File permissions limit who can delete data, which cannot supply the data lost when a hard drive fails.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush installs a service pack on one of the two machines that together run the base e-mail. That machine shuts down completely and takes twenty minutes to restart. Throughout those twenty minutes, users keep sending and reading new mail. Which measure keeps the mail flowing?

keywords.text: two machines that together run the base e-mail

answers.rationale: The service pack is patching, which reduces vulnerabilities, but it cannot carry users' mail while its machine is shut down.
Fault tolerance lets the other drives inside one server supply missing data, but here the whole machine shuts down.
With one of the two machines shut down, the second machine took over the e-mail workload, so users kept getting mail.
Backups restore corrupt or lost data afterward, but users kept getting new mail throughout the twenty minutes.

questions.stem: An airman's only database server has a single hard drive, and a scan shows it lacks the vendor's last two updates, leaving a known weakness. She must keep the database ready for its users while lowering the chance of attack. Which measure should she apply?

keywords.text: lacks the vendor's last two updates

answers.rationale: Clustering needs multiple servers acting as one unit, but this is the airman's only database server.
Applying the vendor's missing updates closes the known weakness, reducing vulnerabilities and the chance of attack while the server stays in use.
Fault tolerance needs multiple drives working together, but this server has a single hard drive.
Backups let her restore lost data, but they do nothing to lower the chance of attack on the known weakness.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush posts a file on a public website that anyone can download, and everyone who opens it sees only an ordinary photo of the flight line. The receiver runs a program on the same file, enters a password and ends up with a short text note. Which method kept the note private?

keywords.text: ends up with a short text note

answers.rationale: Access control limits files to a specific group of users, but this file sits on a public website that anyone can download.
Encryption leaves data in an unreadable format until it is decrypted, yet everyone who opens the file sees an ordinary photo.
Hashing produces a hash value to check that data was not altered; it does not leave the receiver with a text note.
A note drawn out of a file that everyone else sees as an ordinary photo was concealed in the picture.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sets up the unit's file server so that only the finance flight's user accounts can open its pay folders. Other flights' users who try to open them are turned away by the server. The server sits on an open desk in the main office, and the pay records are ordinary spreadsheets. Which measure has he applied?

keywords.text: only the finance flight's user accounts can open its pay folders

answers.rationale: Letting only the finance flight's accounts open the pay folders limits who can reach those files, which helps keep them confidential.
Encryption makes data unreadable until it is decrypted, while here the server turns other flights' users away before they open anything.
Secure area access control locks equipment in closets or secure facilities, but this server sits on an open desk.
Steganography hides information inside a graphic file, but these pay records are ordinary spreadsheets.

questions.stem: An airman does college homework on a government computer and opens an e-mail attachment from a classmate. Weeks later, on a set date, files start vanishing from the drive.
