Only her own account signs on to the computer in her locked office, and it answers requests at its usual speed throughout. What caused the lost files?

keywords.text: on a set date, files start vanishing

answers.rationale: Homework on a government computer can raise a misuse concern, but misuse does not hide for weeks and then delete files.
Unauthorized access needs someone gaining entry remotely or physically, but only her own account signs on, in her locked office.
Denial of service sends a machine more requests than it can handle, but this computer answers requests at its usual speed.
Hidden code that arrived in the attachment, waited for weeks and then activated on a set date to delete files caused the loss.

questions.stem: An airman signs on to a government computer with her own account and downloads a flyer template from a personal website. Against her commander's policy, she prints two hundred flyers for a private car wash on the office printer. The flyers show only the car wash time, place and price. Which concern does her conduct create?

keywords.text: prints two hundred flyers for a private car wash

answers.rationale: Unauthorized access means an unauthorized person gaining entry, but she signed on with her own account.
Printing private car wash flyers on government equipment against the commander's policy uses Air Force resources for a benefit she is not entitled to.
Downloading from a personal website raises the chance of a virus, but the concern here is her own printing of private flyers on government equipment.
Release to unauthorized persons would need sensitive information to leave the office, but the flyers show only the car wash time, place and price.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush learns that a stand-alone classified laptop used to type reports gives off energy from its screen cable and power cord while it runs. An adversary with the right equipment and training could pick up that energy and read the reports on its screen. Which term names that energy?

keywords.text: gives off energy from its screen cable

answers.rationale: Red signals are the plain-text signals partitioned inside cryptographic systems, but this is a stand-alone laptop used to type reports.
Black signals carry encrypted cipher text, while this energy lets an adversary read the reports themselves.
Energy a device gives off without intent, carrying readable data that an adversary with the right equipment could intercept, is the weakness described here.
Intentional transmissions are sent on purpose, but this energy leaks from a screen cable and power cord acting as antennas.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must carry classified traffic over a fiber-optic line between two buildings. The line runs in a plastic carrier whose joints are secured by cleared personnel and inspected under local policy. Its design was set by the facility's threat assessment. Which safeguard is he installing?

keywords.text: plastic carrier whose joints are secured by cleared personnel

answers.rationale: A fiber-optic line in a carrier with joints secured by cleared personnel is the simple form of the safeguard that permits sending classified traffic.
Red/black separation does not apply to fiber optics, and this line is fiber-optic.
A hardened distribution system needs hardened conduit or an alarmed or continuously viewed carrier, not a plastic carrier.
Encryption in transit protects data by scrambling it, while this safeguard relies on a carrier whose joints cleared personnel secure and inspect.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's wing office decides whether a new civilian hire is eligible to see classified material, protects classified drawings released to a company under a classified contract, and safeguards classified reports kept on base. Which choice covers all three of those jobs?

keywords.text: covers all three of those jobs

answers.rationale: Personnel Security covers only the eligibility decision, not drawings released to a company under a classified contract.
Eligibility decisions, protection of material released to industry and protection of classified reports are the three core disciplines of this subset.
Industrial Security covers only material released to industry, not classified reports kept on base.
That discipline protects classified material, but deciding whether a new civilian hire is eligible belongs to another discipline.

questions.stem: An airman applies one set of rules to every system that processes Air Force data, down to office laptops that hold only public web content. The rules guard each system against sabotage, tampering, espionage, and fraud and misuse by each system's own users. Which effort sets these rules?

keywords.text: every system that processes Air Force data

answers.rationale: That discipline protects classified national security information, but these rules reach laptops that hold only public web content.
That program denies unauthorized persons national security information through cryptographic and transmission measures, not by guarding systems against misuse by their own users.
Guarding every Air Force system, whatever its sensitivity, against sabotage, tampering, espionage, fraud and misuse is the scope of this program.
That process guards critical information from adversary observation, not each system against sabotage and tampering.

questions.stem: An airman runs an official system of records, set up under an Air Force directive, that holds living U.S. citizens' Social Security numbers and salaries. The file is already properly marked. A flight member asks to see that member's own entry to check that the salary shown is correct. Which rule sets how he must respond?

answers.rationale: That law gives the general public a right to request agency records, but this member asks for access to that member's own personal entry.
Personal data on living U.S. citizens in an official system of records falls under the law for managing, handling and denying access to such records.
Personnel Security determines eligibility for classified access, but this member only wants to check a salary entry.
That designation concerns safeguarding and marking, but the file is already properly marked.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must store a report in a General Services Administration (GSA) container approved for its level, under continuous guard or an intrusion alarm answered within 15 minutes. He may send it by an approved cryptographic system or by cleared military couriers designated for its level, and any member cleared at its level with a need for it may read it. Which level is the report?

answers.rationale: Secret needs only a container approved for its level, without continuous guard or an alarm answered within 15 minutes.
Confidential needs only a container approved for its level, without continuous guard or an intrusion alarm answered within 15 minutes.
Continuous guard or an alarm answered within 15 minutes, with reading open to any member cleared at that level, marks the highest collateral level.
That control adds special access on top of a collateral level, but any member cleared at this report's level with a need may read it.

questions.stem: An airman's squadron lists the facts about an upcoming deployment that adversaries would most need, and the commander approves the list. It then studies which everyday actions, such as a rise in after-hours parking, an adversary could observe and piece together. The measures it picks include varying shift change times and posting reminders to keep deployment dates off social media. Which effort is the squadron carrying out?

answers.rationale: That program protects communications with cryptographic and transmission measures, while varying shift change times hides an observable routine.
That discipline protects classified material through markings and controls, while these everyday actions are things any outsider could observe.
That program focuses on end points and ports, protocols and services, while after-hours parking is an action outside any computer system.
Listing critical facts, finding observable actions an adversary could piece together and choosing measures to reduce them are the steps of this effort.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's unit plans an exercise and records, at the earliest stage of planning, the exact date, route and number of aircraft that an adversary would vitally need to act against it. The planners decided on these facts in a meeting, and the notes are kept in the unit's locked planning cell. Which term names the date, route and aircraft count?

keywords.text: the exact date, route and number of aircraft

answers.rationale: An indicator is a friendly detectable action an adversary could piece together, but these are facts the planners decided on.
Facts about friendly intentions and capabilities that an adversary vitally needs to plan against the mission are exactly what the unit must protect.
That list is the record that holds such facts and indicators, not the date, route and aircraft count themselves.
Open conversations are one way such facts leak, but these facts stay in notes kept in a locked planning cell.

questions.stem: An airman's office runs its cryptographic equipment exactly by the operating instructions and never discusses the equipment's configuration with uncleared people. It picks a secure telephone for verbal traffic and stores cryptographic material in a General Services Administration (GSA) approved safe whose users are named on an access letter. Which effort is the office following?

answers.rationale: That program manages end points and ports, protocols and services, not the choice of a secure telephone for verbal traffic.
That discipline stores classified material in approved containers, but running cryptographic equipment by its operating instructions belongs elsewhere.
Proper use of cryptographic equipment, choosing a secured system and storing cryptographic material in an approved safe are this program's three components.
That program warns against discussing work with uncleared people, but it does not store cryptographic material under an access letter.

questions.stem: An adversary records a scrambled message that an airman sent over a radio link. Working from guesses about the coding scheme, the adversary tries one approach after another for months until its plain text appears on the adversary's own screen. Which term names the adversary's effort?

keywords.text: tries one approach after another for months

answers.rationale: Working for months from guesses to reveal a scrambled message to an adversary is the science of breaking a coding system.
Decryption restores encrypted data to a readable state for its intended use, but here the plain text appears on an adversary's screen.
Cryptography is the use of coding systems to encrypt and decrypt, but the adversary works from guesses about the coding scheme.
Encryption turns readable data into a scrambled form, but this effort ends with plain text appearing.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush accepts that an enemy may intercept the unit's radio traffic, so he makes sure every message is so skillfully scrambled that intercepted signals stay unreadable to the enemy. He follows the equipment's operating instructions to the letter and discusses the scrambling process only face to face inside the secure area. Which protection is he relying on?

answers.rationale: Choosing the right secured system cannot protect against cryptanalysis, yet here the protection keeps intercepted signals unreadable to the enemy.
Physical barriers, limited access and approved safes guard material, but they do nothing about an enemy intercepting radio traffic.
Cryptography is only the use of coding systems; the protection that comes from using them properly, to the letter of the instructions, goes further.
Proper use of the coding equipment, so intercepted messages stay unreadable and the process is discussed only securely, defeats the enemy's cryptanalysis.

questions.stem: An airman must pass classified details to another base, and he picks the secure telephone over e-mail on the unclassified network. The telephone scrambles his voice as he speaks. The whole task is one phone call from his desk. Which protection does his choice provide?

answers.rationale: Cryptosecurity comes from proper use of the coding equipment, while the protection here comes from picking the secure telephone over the unclassified network.
Selecting the proper secured system for the communication, instead of the unclassified network, is the protection his choice gives.
Physical security deals with safes, barriers and waste destruction, but this task is one phone call from his desk.
Cryptography is the use of coding systems to encrypt, while his step was choosing the secure telephone over e-mail on the unclassified network.

questions.stem: An airman shreds used cryptographic material at the end of each shift. Only cleared people named on a letter for that safe may open the General Services Administration (GSA) approved safe that holds the material, and the safe sits inside a secure area. Which protection is he applying?

answers.rationale: Proper destruction of waste, access limited to cleared people and storage in an approved safe address the handling and viewing threats to cryptographic material.
Cryptosecurity comes from proper use of coding systems, while shredding used material each shift guards against improper destruction of waste.
That component picks the right secured system for a transmission, while a letter naming who may open a safe limits access to material.
That discipline protects classified national security information and its markings, not the destruction of used cryptographic material.

questions.stem: A caller posing as base support talks an airman into reading his password aloud over the phone. Which kind of attack is this?

answers.rationale: A low-technology con that manipulates a person into giving up confidential information fits this call.
Phishing uses fraudulent email, text messages or websites, not a spoken phone call.
Baiting sets a trap that preys on curiosity or greed, such as an infected flash drive.
Unauthorized access reaches a resource through vulnerable system areas, not by talking a person into it.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush traces a break-in to a hacker beyond the base perimeter who guessed a staff password from one home computer. Which threat agent type is this?

answers.rationale: An entity beyond the security perimeter gaining illegitimate entry with a guessed password fits this threat agent.
An inside attack starts within the perimeter by someone granted access, but this hacker is beyond the base perimeter.
A botnet is many compromised computers, but this break-in came from one home computer.
Data diddling changes record entries as a destructive attack; it is not a threat agent.

questions.stem: Radios for a military base pass from the corporation that builds them to a small business that tests them, then to a government agency that delivers them. Which term names this whole arrangement?

answers.rationale: A third party is one intermediary, such as the testing business, not the whole arrangement.
Several entities coordinating to get a product to its destination form this arrangement.
Supply management covers enterprise functions such as sourcing and vendor management, not the entities themselves.
Supply chain security is the effort to protect cargo, not the coordinating entities.

questions.stem: Before radios ship to a base, an airman credentials each carrier crew, screens the crates and fastens them with tamper-proof seals until inspection on entry. Which effort is he carrying out?

answers.rationale: A supply chain is the set of coordinating entities, not the protective steps taken for the cargo.
A third party is an intermediary such as the carrier, not the steps that protect its cargo.
Credentialing participants, screening cargo, sealing it in transit and inspecting it on entry are typical activities of this effort.
Third party data storage concerns an outside provider holding data, not crates of radios.

questions.stem: When an airman opens a spreadsheet, code written in the program's task-automation language runs on its own and emails everyone in his address book. Which kind of malicious code is this?

answers.rationale: A file infector attaches to executable files and loads with them, not as automation code in a spreadsheet.
Code in an application's automation language, triggered when someone opens the file, fits this kind.
A boot-sector virus lives in a disk's first sector and runs at startup, not when a file opens.
A logic bomb waits for a certain event such as a date, not the opening of a file.

questions.stem: An airman's account has full control over all the hardware, software and firmware operations that run the unit's cyber systems. Which classification does his account hold?

answers.rationale: User access gives only selected control, such as email and share drives, not full control.
Unauthorized access reaches a resource a machine should not provide, and nothing says this account is improper.
Full rights over all hardware, software and firmware operations mark this classification.
Elevation of privilege is a threat that allows unauthorized actions, not a classification of accounts.

questions.stem: During a design review with Microsoft's threat model, an airman flags a flaw that lets one sender use up a host's memory and processing power so no one else can log on. Which category is that?

answers.rationale: Tampering modifies something on a disk, network or memory, while this flaw only uses resources up.
Information disclosure gives information to someone unauthorized, but nothing is revealed here.
Elevation of privilege lets someone do unauthorized actions, while this sender only exhausts resources.
Exhausting the resources a host needs so that others cannot use it fits this category.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's network screens every device before it joins and checks every logon, yet one unsafe program he installed lets a hacker get around all of it. Which area of protection did he overlook?

answers.rationale: Screening each device before it joins was in place; the weakness came from a program he installed.
Every logon was checked; the weakness was an installed program, not a failed logon check.
Ensuring the integrity of installed software keeps one unsafe program from undoing the other defenses.
Hardware security covers physical devices and boot threats, not an unsafe program he installed.

questions.stem: A tool watching base traffic spots a flood of odd packets and, within a second, shuts off their source on its own. Which tool acted?

keywords.text: shuts off their source on its own

answers.rationale: This logs and alerts on what it finds, leaving any response to an administrator.
This analyzes traffic across many systems and sends alerts, but it does not shut off a source.
A sensor only collects segment traffic and forwards it; it does not act against the source.
Watching traffic and then cutting off the source on its own is corrective action.

questions.stem: BitLocker protects every byte of a laptop's drive, keeping it unreadable to a thief. Which component holds the cryptographic keys BitLocker uses?

answers.rationale: When a whole drive is protected this way, this module stores the keys used to protect the data.
This add-on card holds cryptographic processors; it is not the part BitLocker uses for its keys.
Secure boot lets only digitally signed bootup files run; it does not store BitLocker's keys.
This chip holds code that interfaces with the hardware, not the keys used to protect the drive.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants to add crypto processors to a server by plugging in their own extra board. Which choice fits his plan?

answers.rationale: This module stores cryptographic keys for drive protection, not an extra board of crypto processors.
An add-on device that places cryptographic processors on a separate card installed in the server fits this plan.
Software encryption runs as programs, not on an extra board of crypto processors.
This protects an entire drive in case of theft or loss; it is not an extra processor board.

questions.stem: Compliance software stays installed on each base laptop and keeps checking it all day, long after it connects. Which kind of software is this?

answers.rationale: Software that remains on the laptop and monitors it continuously is the kind that stays installed.
These run the check when a device connects, then remove themselves instead of staying installed.
Agentless checks put no software on the laptop; the authentication server performs them.
These scan for updates and antivirus when a system connects; they are not software that stays.

questions.stem: After typing her password, an airman types a six-digit number that just arrived by text message on her phone. Which factor does that number add?

answers.rationale: Her password is the known secret; the number proves she holds the phone it was sent to.
Codes sent to a mobile phone by text message prove she possesses a physical object.
This factor reads habits such as typing patterns, not a number sent to her phone.
Combining factors is the overall scheme; the question asks which single factor the number adds.

questions.stem: Group policy changes made on a Windows Server reach every workstation in the domain every 90 minutes, at next logon and on restart. Through which service are they centrally configured?

answers.rationale: This names the set of group policy configurations being changed, not the service that delivers them.
Group policy is centrally configured through this service on Windows Server, which applies it every 90 minutes.
Local Policies hold user rights, auditing and banners inside a policy set, not the service that delivers changes.
A proxy server sits between workstations and the Internet to filter web sites, not to deliver group policy.

questions.stem: A program an airman adds to her laptop drops packets sent to that laptop from the Internet. Which type of protection is this?

answers.rationale: A hardware-based firewall sits at the network edge, while this is a program added to one laptop.
A packet-filtering firewall is a hardware type at the network edge, while this is a program on one laptop.
A proxy server sits between users' computers and the Internet, while this program guards one laptop.
A program added to her laptop that drops packets sent to it protects that single system.

questions.stem: An airman writes firewall rules for traffic from the Internet and from a network a partner organization's administrators run. In the firewall plan, where does this traffic come from?

answers.rationale: An extranet holds base servers for selected organizations, while this traffic comes from networks others run.
The area between two firewalls is the base's own, while this traffic starts on networks others run.
A guest zone is the base's own area for office visitors, while this traffic starts on outside networks.
The Internet and a partner's network both lie outside the control of her base's administrators.

questions.stem: An airman spots that a base web server answered slowly for two minutes overnight, then ran normally, and starts her first report. What should she call it for now?

answers.rationale: An incident is an occurrence assessed as risking a system or its data, and she has only just spotted this.
Any occurrence seen on a system counts as this until assessed, and she is only starting her first report.
A denial of service attack is a named incident type, which takes an assessment beyond her first report.
A root cause is the reason behind an incident found during analysis, not a name for something just seen.

questions.stem: An airman spots questionable activity in her unit's service management records as an intrusion sensor flags the same traffic, and she passes these first details up. Which phase is this?

answers.rationale: Preliminary analysis and identification categorizes the activity, but she has only spotted it and passed the first details up.
Preliminary response actions contain the threat and preserve data, but she has only spotted the activity and passed it up.
Incident analysis studies technical details and root cause, but she has only spotted the activity and passed it up.
Spotting questionable activity through records and sensors and passing the first details up is phase one.

questions.stem: During analysis of a breach, an airman has one hour to decide whether commanders must be told of it under their critical information criteria. Which analysis step is he performing?

answers.rationale: Validating reviews and corroborates the reported details, not whether commanders must be told within an hour.
This plan element tells users when and how to speak up before any breach, not an hour-limited analysis step.
Deciding within one hour whether a breach meets commanders' critical information criteria is this analysis step.
Determining operational impact weighs harm to the mission, not whether commanders must be told within an hour.

questions.stem: A server's operating software sees one single drive, but the data actually sits on three physical drives grouped for safety and speed. Which technology is this?

answers.rationale: Electronic vaulting is a backup method, not a way to make several drives appear as one.
It manages drives so that one logical drive is built from several physical drives, safer and faster.
Network storage devices are a kind of backup media, not drives grouped to appear as one.
Striping uses two drives with no redundancy, so it gives speed but not safety.

questions.stem: An airman keeps every site logon in an encrypted wallet program, and one strong secret of many characters, used nowhere else, unlocks it. Which term names that secret?

answers.rationale: That card is something she carries, not a secret she knows that unlocks the wallet program.
A username names an account but is not the secret that unlocks the wallet.
That software is the wallet program itself, not the secret that unlocks it.
One strong secret, not reused anywhere, protects the encrypted wallet that holds all her other logons.

questions.stem: A unit runs one large copy job each Sunday and wants each weeknight job to copy as little data as possible. Which type should the weeknight jobs be?

answers.rationale: Copying only what changed since the previous night keeps each job small, and daily jobs are normally this type.
A full job copies all selected files, the most data possible, which suits the large Sunday job.
A differential job copies everything changed since Sunday, so each weeknight job grows larger.
Mirroring reflects every save onto a second drive at once; it is not a nightly copy job.

questions.stem: A file server keeps its data on several hard drives that work together. When one drive dies, the airman's files still open because the remaining disks supply what was lost. Which availability solution is in place?

answers.rationale: Clustering joins several servers so one takes over for another, not several drives inside one file server.
Patching applies updates to close weaknesses; it does not supply data from a dead drive.
Backups restore data after it is lost, but here the files still open right after the drive dies.
Drives working together so the rest supply a failed drive's data is this data redundancy solution.

questions.stem: Every month an airman installs the vendor's newest service updates on a server to close weaknesses that attackers could use. Which availability solution is she performing?

answers.rationale: Installing the newest updates to close weaknesses attackers could use keeps the server current and less open to attack.
Backups copy data so it can be restored, but they do not close weaknesses attackers could use.
Clustering adds servers that take over for each other; it does not close weaknesses on one server.
Permissions limit who can delete data; installing vendor updates to close weaknesses is a different solution.

questions.stem: On a shared server folder, an airman builds a list of the user accounts allowed to open each file, so only his flight can read them. Which confidentiality method is he using?

answers.rationale: Encryption scrambles file contents until decrypted; a list of allowed accounts is a different method.
A list of accounts allowed to open each file, set on the folder, is this way of setting permissions.
Steganography hides data inside a graphic file; nothing here is hidden inside a picture.
Password protection makes one person enter a code to log on, not a list of accounts for each file.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds that an airman printed a stack of church car wash flyers on the duty section's government printer. Which threat to government computer resources does this show?

answers.rationale: Malicious logic is code written to harm a computer, and printing flyers involves no harmful code.
Unauthorized access is a hacker or intruder getting into a system, but here the problem is personal printing.
Steal-ware is a kind of malicious code on a computer, not personal flyers printed on a government printer.
Using a government printer and supplies for personal flyers gives an individual a benefit they are not entitled to.

questions.stem: An airman keeps the unit's cryptographic keying material in an approved safe within a secure area. Only people named on that safe's own access letter may open it. Which component of protecting communications is she practicing?

answers.rationale: A safe in a secure area that only listed people may open limits who can reach the material.
Cryptosecurity is the proper use of cryptographic systems, not where the keying material is locked up.
This component picks the right secured system for sending messages; storing material in a safe is something else.
Cryptanalysis is the science of breaking a coding system, not a way to guard material.

questions.stem: Members of the public write to a federal agency asking for copies of its records on a base project. The agency must hand them over unless one of nine exemptions applies. Which law gives them this right?

answers.rationale: The Privacy Act of 1974 governs personal records in a system of records, not public requests for agency records.
This designation marks unclassified information needing controls; it is not a law giving the public a right to records.
This legacy marking flags unclassified information that may be withheld, not a law giving the public records.
A law giving the public access to federal agency records, unless one of nine exemptions applies, is this act.

questions.stem: An airman maintains an official file of living members' Social Security numbers, ages and salaries. Which law sets how she must manage, handle and deny access to these personal records?

answers.rationale: This law lets the public request agency records; it does not set how personal records are managed.
A law on managing, handling and denying access to personal records kept on living citizens is this act.
This is a designation for unclassified information needing controls, not a law on managing personal records.
This legacy marking may appear on such records, but it is a marking, not the law that governs them.

questions.stem: Adversaries record a scrambled radio message and spend weeks guessing at its coding scheme until the plain text appears on their screen. Which term names their effort?

answers.rationale: Spending weeks guessing at a coding scheme so outsiders can read the message is this science.
Decryption restores data to plain text for an authorized person, not outsiders guessing at the scheme.
Cryptography is using coding systems to encrypt and decrypt, not attacking a scheme by guessing.
Cryptosecurity is the protection from using cryptographic systems properly, which these adversaries are trying to defeat.

questions.stem: Reviewing a design with Microsoft's threat model, an airman finds a public page listing personnel records that only the personnel office may see. Which category is this flaw?

answers.rationale: A public page showing records only the personnel office may see provides them to people not authorized to have them.
Elevation of privilege lets someone do unauthorized actions, but anyone opening this page only reads it.
Spoofing is pretending to be someone else, but this flaw is a page showing records to anyone.
Tampering modifies something, but this page only shows the records as they are.

questions.stem: A base logon program, built with a mistake, accepts any password after three failed tries. Its logs show only normal logons so far. Which term names this mistake?

answers.rationale: A threat is a possible danger that may exploit the mistake, not the mistake itself.
A weakness in how a program was built that could be exploited, with only normal logons so far, fits here.
A network attack is an intentional act, but the logs show only normal logons so far.
Software patching would repair the mistake; it does not name the mistake itself.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush learns that a hacker deliberately got around the base's security controls and broke its security policy to reach stored records. Which term names what the hacker did?

answers.rationale: A threat is only a possible danger, while this hacker actually acted.
A vulnerability is a flaw the hacker may have used, not the deliberate act itself.
A deliberate act by an intelligent actor to evade security controls and break policy fits this term.
Malicious code is software or scripts, not the hacker's own deliberate act.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush groups two break-ins under one attack type: one quietly altered pay records, and the other erased a whole drive. Which type covers both?

answers.rationale: Unauthorized access aims to reach a resource, not to alter or erase what is stored.
Denial of Service floods a machine with requests, and neither break-in did that.
Executing commands illicitly is an untrusted person running commands on a server, not altering or erasing records.
Changing record entries and getting rid of stored files are its two major categories.

questions.stem: After an airman installs a free game, sale offers pop up on her screen every few minutes, while her files open normally. Which program is causing this?

answers.rationale: Spyware secretly sends user information to a remote system, while these sale offers appear openly on her screen.
Ransomware locks the screen or files until a ransom is paid, but her files open normally.
Software that automatically loads sale offers in pop-ups on the screen fits this program.
A rootkit gives a hacker hidden privileged access, not visible pop-up offers.

questions.stem: An airman's unit wants to cut hardware costs by moving its in-house file services off-site to a cloud provider. Which supply chain concern must she check first?

answers.rationale: Compromised hardware or software comes from ordering new products, but the unit is cutting hardware, not buying it.
Supply management covers enterprise functions such as sourcing, not an outside provider holding the unit's files.
Supply chain security protects cargo in transit, and no cargo is being shipped.
Moving in-house services off-site puts possibly sensitive files with an outside provider, whose protection must be confirmed first.

questions.stem: An attacker uses names found on social media to email only the members of one base's finance flight, posing as their own payroll office. Which type of con is this?

answers.rationale: Targeting one specific group with messages that appeal to it, using names from public sources, fits this con.
Whaling targets high-value individuals such as a company board member, not a whole finance flight.
Baiting uses curiosity or greed, such as an infected flash drive, not a spoofed email to named members.
Unauthorized access reaches a resource through vulnerable system areas, not through a deceiving email.

questions.stem: After a server confirms an airman's identity, she can open the training folder, while the finance folder stays locked to her. Which step decided what she could open?

keywords.text: the finance folder stays locked to her

answers.rationale: Authentication confirmed her identity; that happened before any folder opened or stayed locked.
Once her identity is verified, this step grants only the tasks she is permitted, such as the training folder.
Accounting logs her activity and the resources she uses; it does not decide which folders open.
Identification is presenting a username or smartcard; it does not decide which folders she may open.

questions.stem: An airman wants a laptop's stored data scrambled in a very complex way at the highest speed, using the laptop's own built-in parts. Which approach is this?

keywords.text: using the laptop's own built-in parts

answers.rationale: Chips physically installed in the system apply very complex scrambling more quickly than software does.
Software encryption is the slower kind done by a program, while this work needs the highest speed.
This is one add-on card holding crypto processors, not the general approach of chips doing fast scrambling.
This module stores cryptographic keys for whole-drive protection; it does not itself do the fast scrambling.

questions.stem: Software on one workstation notices an attack on that workstation and halts it on the spot, with no airman stepping in. Which tool is this?

answers.rationale: This runs on one workstation too, but it only shows or emails notifications for review.
This watches traffic across many systems and alerts; it does not halt an attack on one workstation.
Software on one workstation that stops attacks on it without anyone stepping in fits this tool.
This detects, logs and alerts, but it does not halt the attack itself.

questions.stem: An airman's plan for the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) forbids going back to design work once coding starts, because backtracking is judged too costly. Which model is the team following?

answers.rationale: Agile allows backtracking as necessary, but this plan forbids going back.
Implementation is the phase where code gets written, not the model that forbids going back.
Each phase must finish before the next, and backtracking is not permitted because it is costly.
Fuzzing feeds random invalid data to test for crashes; it is not a model of phases.

questions.stem: Within a Network-Based Intrusion Detection System (NIDS), one component receives packets gathered from each segment and judges whether they are suspicious. Which component is it?

answers.rationale: A sensor collects traffic on its own segment and forwards it; it does not judge the packets.
A collector gathers traffic from the sensors and passes it on without judging it.
The console receives alerts and is where the whole tool is configured; it does not judge packets.
This component receives packets from the sensor or collector and performs the analysis that flags suspicious ones.

questions.stem: An airman needs a newer centralized logon protocol for a base with several makers' devices, sending every request over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). Which protocol fits?

keywords.text: sending every request over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)

answers.rationale: This sends its requests over User Datagram Protocol (UDP), a different transport from the one required.
This newer protocol gives a more reliable and secure communication service over that transport.
This is the protocol used in modern Cisco networks, while this base mixes devices from several makers.
This lets users log on once for many systems; it is not a request protocol.

questions.stem: An airman secures reports on a Windows server in two steps: first with rights set on the drive itself, then again when she publishes them to the network. Which category of access control is she building?

answers.rationale: Securing the drive, then publishing the folder to the network, are the two steps of this category.
Networking lists regulate inbound and outbound traffic at a router, not reports secured on a server's drive.
This category is a directory service storing information about network resources, not rights set on a drive.
This is a set of group policy configurations, not a category of access control for reports.

questions.stem: Whenever a system on the network attempts a connection to an airman's workstation, its firewall puts an alert on his screen. Which common firewall feature produced the alert?

answers.rationale: Blocking incoming traffic drops packets sent to the system; it does not put an alert on the screen.
Creating rules customizes what traffic may enter or exit; it does not itself alert the airman.
Showing a message when someone attempts to connect to the system is the job of this feature.
The default rule denies all traffic unless allowed; it does not put an alert on his screen.

questions.stem: A base's firewall plan splits its systems into separate parts for staff, servers and visitors. What is the purpose of splitting them this way?

keywords.text: splits its systems into separate parts

answers.rationale: Giving visitors Internet access only is the job of one guest zone, not the purpose of every split.
Splitting staff, servers and visitors into parts lets the firewall decide what may pass from one part to another.

answers.text: Let the public reach web servers
answers.rationale: Letting the public reach web servers is the job of the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) alone, not the whole split.
Sharing servers with selected organizations is what an extranet does, not why every part is split off.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush asks the breached server's communications focal point and network operations and security center how critical that server is rated for the mission. Which analysis step is this?

keywords.text: how critical that server is rated

answers.rationale: Working with the server's owning support agencies to learn its Mission Assurance Category level is this analysis step.
Determining operational impact weighs damage to the mission, while he asks how critical the server is rated.
Gathering information collects logs and accounts, but he asks these agencies how critical the server is rated.
Validating reviews and corroborates the reported breach, but his calls ask how critical the server is rated.

questions.stem: Reviewers confirm that someone who guessed a password entered a base file server and copied private records to an outside computer. What has this been assessed as?

answers.rationale: An event is any observable occurrence, but this one has been reviewed and confirmed to expose private records.
A denial of service attack disrupts normal function, while this breach exposed private records to an outside computer.
A reviewed occurrence that exposed private records jeopardizes confidentiality, so the assessment names it this.
A social engineering attack tricks a person, but here the password was guessed without tricking anyone.

questions.stem: An airman tells the response staff that a phone call tricked him into giving his password. The staff look up which named type of attack this is in their plan, so they can react the right way. Which plan element are they using?

answers.rationale: Looking up which named attack type this is, such as social engineering, uses the types the plan defines.
Reporting requirements say when and how users speak up, but he already has and staff need the type.
Roles and responsibilities give each member's job, not which named type of attack this is.
Exercise planning sets practice drills, but this is a real call and the staff need its type.

questions.stem: An airman lets his antivirus update, restarts when prompted, keeps a different long password for each site and backs up his files each week. A briefing says that if every user kept up small steps like these, most attacks would fail. Which term names what he keeps up?

answers.rationale: Configuration management keeps systems, servers and software in a reliable, consistent state by tracking every change; it is not one user's regular steps.
A baseline configuration is the recorded starting point for later assessments, not a set of steps a user repeats.
Practices a user repeats to maintain system health and improve online security, such as updates, strong passwords and backups, are cyber hygiene.
Virus definitions are what the antivirus update brings in; they are one part of his steps, not the name for all of them.

questions.stem: One of a server's two drives fails, and an airman replaces it while the other drive still holds every file exactly as it was saved. Which Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) setup was the server using?

keywords.text: every file exactly as it was saved

answers.rationale: Level 0 divides data between the drives with no copy, so one failure loses all of it.
With two drives that each hold an exact duplicate, the surviving drive still has every file.
Level 1+0 needs at least four disks, and this server has only two drives.
Level 5 needs at least three disks and rebuilds lost data from parity, but this server has two.

questions.stem: Base administrators regularly send new data out to every user's antivirus so it stays effective, and each user restarts when prompted. Which item are the administrators sending?

answers.rationale: Software patches fix security problems in the software itself; they are not data for the antivirus.
Security scans are checks the antivirus runs, not data administrators send to it.
For antivirus software to stay effective, administrators must regularly push this updated information out to users.
Firewall settings are managed by administrators and control network traffic, not what antivirus detects.

questions.stem: An airman must send a short report so that anyone who opens the file sees only a vacation photo. At the other end, a special application pulls the report back out. Which way of keeping data confidential is the airman using?

answers.rationale: Tucking the report inside an ordinary-looking photo and pulling it out with an application is this hiding method.
Encryption makes the report unreadable, but the file would not look like a normal vacation photo.
Access control limits who may open a file; it does not make the report look like a photo.
Hashing checks that data was not changed; it does not hide a report inside a photo.

questions.stem: An airman saved a report on the shared drive last month. Today he compares it word for word with that day's printout. Which goal is he checking?

answers.rationale: Confidentiality keeps unauthorized people from reading the report, not proving that its words are unchanged.
Being certain that stored data still matches what was saved, word for word, is this goal of the triad.
Availability makes sure the report can be opened when wanted, not that its words match the printout.
Nonrepudiation stops a sender from denying a message, but this airman only needs to know the saved report is unchanged.

questions.stem: A base e-mail service runs on several servers that work as a single unit. When one crashes, users keep sending mail as usual. Which availability solution is in place?

answers.rationale: Fault tolerance spreads data across several drives, not a service across several servers that work as one.
Backups let lost data be restored later, but here users keep sending mail as usual when the server crashes.
Several servers working as one, with a survivor carrying the load when one crashes, is this high-availability solution.
Patching applies updates to reduce weaknesses; it does not let another server pick up the work.

questions.stem: An airman locks the unit's switches and routers in a centralized communications closet. He also stores removable hard disks in a classified approved safe when they are taken out of the system. Which protection against intruders is he applying?

answers.rationale: Password protection asks for a code before logon, but locking a closet and a safe are physical steps.
File permissions limit which accounts open files; they do not lock routers or disks away physically.
Locking network gear in a closet and disks in an approved safe are physical steps that keep intruders out.
Encryption in storage makes data unreadable; it does not lock switches, routers or disks away.

questions.stem: An airman runs a fiber-optic line between two buildings to carry classified plain-text data. Physical, acoustical and electromagnetic safeguards on it make that use allowed. What is this line called?

answers.rationale: Red/black separation keeps plain-text signals apart from encrypted ones in copper cabling, but this line is fiber-optic.
A fiber-optic line with safeguards that let classified data travel as plain text is this countermeasure.
Shielding of equipment reduces stray signals from devices, not a safeguarded line built to carry unencrypted data.
Encryption in transit scrambles data on the line, but this data travels as plain text.

questions.stem: In a room of cryptographic gear wired with copper cable, MSgt Rush keeps the lines carrying readable classified text well apart from the lines carrying scrambled cipher text. Which principle is he following?

answers.rationale: A protected distribution system is a safeguarded line for unencrypted data, not keeping readable and scrambled lines apart.
Shielding places a protective agent around equipment or circuits, but here the lines are simply kept well apart.
Keeping readable classified signals apart from scrambled cipher signals in copper cabling is this principle.
Cryptosecurity is using cryptographic systems properly, not how readable and scrambled lines are kept apart.

questions.stem: A recall roster lists each airman's home phone number and address. After hours it may sit in an unlocked desk in a guarded building. Which designation fits it?

answers.rationale: An unclassified roster of personal details, kept in an unlocked desk in a guarded building, fits this designation.
Confidential material needs an approved security container, but this roster may sit in an unlocked desk.
Secret material needs an approved security container, but this roster may sit in an unlocked desk.
Top Secret material needs a container under guard or alarm, but this roster may sit in an unlocked desk.

questions.stem: If a classified report leaked, the harm to the nation's security would be more than some damage but less than exceptionally grave. Which classification level is it?

answers.rationale: Top Secret leaks could cause exceptionally grave damage, but this report's harm would be less than that.
Harm above some damage but below exceptionally grave matches this middle level and its substantial degree of protection.
Confidential leaks could cause some damage, but this report's harm would be more than that.
This designation is not a classification level, and the report is described as classified.
